And when he entered the church,
not while standing,
but while prostrate, he was praying and saying:
"My soul clings to the dust;
revive me according to Your word."
And in the thirteenth year of Theodosius, he proclaimed Arcadius his son king in the East.
And two years later Eugenius and Argobastes (Arbogast?) in Rome deceived the chamberlain of Valentinian,
and he strangled the king.
And when Theodosius heard, he hastened and appointed Honorius, his younger son, king in the West,
and he went against the tyrant Eugenius,
and he defeated the great army of the barbarians that was with him.
And when the barbarians saw that they were defeated, they cried out and asked for pardon.
And the king ordered that they bring down (bring?) the tyrant.
And they ran, seized him,
and when bound, brought him to the king,
and he was killed.
And Argobastes strangled himself.
And after these things, when the king returned to Mediolini (to Mediolanum? [Milan]):
from the fatigue of battle he became sick and died.
And in that same year Yazdegerd, the son of Shapur, reigned over the Persians for twenty-one years.
After Theodosius the Great, his sons Arcadius and Honorius {OCR?} reigned for thirteen years.
While Arcadius was reigning in Constantinople and in the East,
Honorius, a boy of nine years, was king in Rome.
And in that same year, in Tammuz, the Huns {OCR?} went out against the territory of the Romans,
and they devastated and took captives from Syria and Cappadocia,
which is the year seven hundred and eight of Alexander (397 of our Lord?).
And Arcadius built the great colonnade (ambolōn?) which is in front of the Praetorium;
and also Eudoxia his wife erected a silver statue near the neighborhood of Saint Irene.
And Gainas, who rebelled against him, he defeated and killed.
